# The appointments Ṛta made — and who is keeping them

The mistake is reading myths as entertainment. Ṛta's cycle reads more like a charter — each story assigning a duty the modern world still pays for.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Ṛta
- **Pantheon:** Sanskrit
- **Domain of influence:** Cosmic Order, Truth, Law
- **Pattern seats:** 4
- **Sectors touched:** Commerce & Governance · Energy & Natural World · Culture & Entertainment · Society & Spirit
- **Strongest seat:** Legal, Justice & Compliance
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 210 of 271

## The Cycle, Read Forward

### Legal, Justice & Compliance — through *The Chariot of the Sun*

In Ṛgvedic hymns, the sun's chariot is said to roll by Ṛta.  The seven horses, the wheel, and the path are all fitted together by this principle.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Cosmic order and law; the Vedic name of justice.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. That is the cycle working: story becomes duty, duty becomes trade.

### Environmental & Climate Services — through *True Speech*

Ṛta is closely linked to satya, truth.  A true statement is one that is ṛta — rightly joined to reality.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *India's environmental thinkers have reclaimed ṛta as the name for ecological balance.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. The trade thinks it is optimizing a process. It is re-enacting a charter.

### Timekeeping & Calendar Systems — through *Even the Gods Obey*

Unlike the sovereign gods of Near Eastern mythologies, the Vedic gods are not above cosmic law.  Indra, Agni, and Varuṇa act within Ṛta and are praised for upholding it.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *The seasons turn by ṛta, and ṛtu — the Sanskrit word for season — is its own child.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. Industries do not invent their archetypes; they inherit them and call them best practice.

### Philosophy, Ethics & Standards — through *The Chariot of the Sun*

In Ṛgvedic hymns, the sun's chariot is said to roll by Ṛta.  The seven horses, the wheel, and the path are all fitted together by this principle.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Cosmic order as moral law.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. The trade thinks it is optimizing a process. It is re-enacting a charter.

## The Theme That Runs the Cycle

Ṛta has no personal mythology — no birth, no love affairs, no wars. Its 'stories' are the regular events of the cosmos: dawn after night, rain after drought, the fire rising when the priest kindles it.

## The Method, Stated Plainly

Skeptical? Good — the system is built for you. Every seat in this file carries its why-line and its weight, the full derivation is public at the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/), and the challenge process is part of the design. Falsifiable is not a posture here; it is the mechanism.

## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in legal, justice & compliance, environmental & climate services, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/sites/rta/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit.
